options.value: They go to a warehouse, then out to shops.

Because the key's frame changed, the en-minimal-pair-skim distractor no longer differed from it by one detail; it is rewritten as the key's frame with Reuben swapped for Ilya (Ilya's sock, line 28), so the tag names its mistake again.

options.value: By showing what Ilya does with things, like the football sock.

options.value: He describes only the old clothes, and so we get nothing else.

options.value: By showing what he does with things, like the jumper and the paper.

options.execution: True at line 34, and it is how he got there rather than why he woke.

options.value: He had to find out what made every noise.
He sat on all of their laps in turn.
options.execution: True at lines 38 and 39, at breakfast the next morning. The child answers from the morning, but lines 34 to 36 give what kept him up in the night.

options.value: He was keeping watch on the door for the family.
options.execution: A restless animal invites a guard; no line gives him one.

rebuilds.why: The execution on 'A garden that somebody keeps tidy for him' said 'only half cultivated, so nobody is keeping it', but half cultivated means half of it is kept. The exclusion now rests on 'for him'. walkScript placed 'his tail grew bottle-brushy' at line 45; it runs across lines 44 and 45, now cited as such. Nothing else changed.

stem.text: Look at lines 41 to 46. What does the garden mean to Rikki-tikki at first?

options.value: It was large and only half looked after.
options.execution: Reuses lines 41 and 42 and describes it rather than saying what it means.

options.value: A thorn-bush with sorrowful voices in it.
options.execution: True at line 46, and it is what stops him rather than the garden.

options.value: A place with plenty in it for him to hunt.
A garden that somebody keeps tidy for him.
options.execution: Nothing in lines 41 to 46 says the garden is kept for Rikki-tikki, who has only just arrived. The child supplies a keeper working for him, which the passage never gives.

explanationPatch.walkScript: Line 44 has him lick his lips at the garden. Line 44 calls it a splendid hunting-ground. Lines 44 and 45 say his tail grew bottle-brushy.

rebuilds.why: passageRef was missing: stem.passageRef set to stream-a-15-jungle-book. The stem already cites lines 47 to 50, lineRefs [47,48,49,50] stand, and every distractor already has an execution (checked against the lines). Nothing else changed.

stem.text: Look at lines 47 to 50. How had Darzee and his wife made their nest?

options.value: By swaying it to and fro as they sat on the rim.
options.execution: True at line 49, and the swaying is the nest rather than their work.

options.value: By wrapping it in cotton wool over a little fire.
options.execution: Lines 15 and 16 are where the family wrap Rikki-tikki in cotton wool and warm him over a little fire. The child carries that care of the mongoose across to the birds' nest, helped by the cotton that does fill the nest at line 49.

options.value: By tying it to the thorn-bush with fibres.
options.execution: Line 48 names what the leaves were stitched with; no line ties the nest to anything.

options.value: By stitching two big leaves together at the edges.

rebuilds.why: The execution on 'Because they had already told him about the baby' claimed line 55 answers the stem by quoting the literal-lookalike's restatement. It now gives the real reason, the hiss at lines 55 and 56. Nothing else changed.

stem.text: Look at lines 55 to 58. Why do Darzee and his wife not answer?

options.value: They cowered down in the nest without answering.
options.execution: Reuses line 55 and repeats them rather than giving a reason.

options.value: Because the snake was in the grass below their nest.
Because the hiss made Rikki-tikki jump back.
options.execution: True at lines 56 and 57, and it is about him rather than them.

options.value: Because they had already told him about the baby.
options.execution: True at lines 52 and 53, before the hiss came. The child answers from the earlier talk, but lines 55 and 56 give the hiss from the grass as the reason they say nothing.

rebuilds.why: The en-whole-text-absence-asserted distractor 'The writer says each time that Rikki-tikki is only proving the rule' was partly defensible, because lines 39 and 68 do tie his acts to the rule, and its execution called them 'without comment', which is false. The option is replaced with 'The writer says Rikki-tikki is not like other mongooses at all.', tagged en-contradicted-by-the-text: line 21 says he 'was a true mongoose'. Key, other options, hint and walk script unchanged.

stem.text: Think about the whole passage. What does the writer keep doing with mongooses?

options.value: A motto is given for the whole mongoose family, and it says run and find out.
options.execution: Reuses line 20 and quotes the rule instead of naming the pattern.

options.value: Rikki-tikki is braver, but he is still the youngest of his family.
options.execution: A ranking across the whole passage that no line makes.

options.value: The writer says Rikki-tikki is not like other mongooses at all.
options.execution: Line 21 says Rikki-tikki was a true mongoose, and lines 39 and 68 tie what he does to every mongoose. The child takes the hero of the story to be unlike the rest, which the passage states the contrary of.

options.value: A rule about all mongooses is given, but Rikki-tikki is the one who does it.
